title: Flood Advisory
description: ...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in Texas... Los Olmos Creek Near Falfurrias affecting Brooks County. .The river gauge at Los Olmos Creek near Falfurrias continues to fall steadily this afternoon, and is now expected to drop below action stage early Friday morning. The latest forecast has gauge levels falling well below bankfull over the weekend, and remaining so into early next week. For the Los Olmos Creek...including Falfurrias...elevated river levels are forecast. * WHAT...Minor flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues along the creek banks. * WHERE...Los Olmos Creek near Falfurrias. * WHEN...Until Friday morning. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 12:15 PM CST Thursday the stage was 6.85 feet and falling. - Bankfull stage is 5.0 feet. - The level has fallen from 8.7 feet at 5 PM Wednesday to below 7 feet just before noon Thursday. - Forecast...The river is expected to fall to 2.1 feet early Tuesday afternoon, November 17th. - Action stage is 5.0 feet. - Flood stage is 11.0 feet. - https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

title: Flood Advisory
description: * WHAT...Coastal Flooding from abnormally high tides. * WHERE...Low-lying areas along the San Pablo Bay, Carquinez Strait, and Suisun Bay shorelines in Solano County. * WHEN...Until 400 PM PST Friday. * IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots, roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 937 AM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding. - The highest tides forecast each day are (all times local time): * Port Chicago: 1.2 ft above normal (6.1 ft MLLW) at 2:15 PM Thu 11/12, 1.0 ft above normal (5.9 ft MLLW) at 2:56 PM Fri 11/13, 0.7 ft above normal (5.6 ft MLLW) at 3:44 PM Sat 11/14, and 0.3 ft above normal (5.2 ft MLLW) at 4:39 PM Sun 11/15. * West Sacramento: 1.2 ft above normal (5.5 ft MLLW) at 5:28 PM Thu 11/12, 1.0 ft above normal (5.4 ft MLLW) at 6:10 PM Fri 11/13, 0.9 ft above normal (5.2 ft MLLW) at 6:57 PM Sat 11/14, and 0.6 ft above normal (5.0 ft MLLW) at 7:50 PM Sun 11/15. * Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.5 ft at 5:00 PM Thu 11/12, +7.7 ft at 5:00 PM Fri 11/13, and +7.6 ft at 6:00 PM Sat 11/14. - These predictions include up to +1.1 feet of storm surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. Timing of high tide may vary up to an hour throughout the San Francisco Bay and Delta. - Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at: * Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre dictions.html?id=9415144 * West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide predictions.html?id=9416131 * Rio Vista: https://water.noaa.gov/gauges/RVBC1

title: Flood Warning
description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties. .River levels on the St Johns at Astor are forecast continue a steady decline in Minor Flood Stage through Friday, then northerly winds and downstream tidal effects this weekend are expected to slow or halt the decline. Rises from upstream heavy heavy rainfall are possible as water works through the basin. For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Astor. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud roads are underwater with yards inundated. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 8:30 PM EST Thursday the stage was 2.7 feet. - Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 8:30 PM EST Thursday was 2.7 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to continue a gradual decline through Friday, then he decline is forecast to slow or halt this weekend. Additional rises are possible thereafter. - Flood stage is 2.3 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

title: Flood Warning
description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County. .Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns near Geneva Above Lake Harney to reach Moderate flood stage. River levels may fluctuate slightly, but are forecast to generally remain around 9.1 feet through the weekend and into next week. For the St. Johns River...Above Lake Harney...Moderate flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Water enters the first story of homes on Whitcomb Drive between Crossover Lane and Lake Harney Road. Water covers Mullet Lake Park. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 7:30 PM EST Thursday the stage was 9.1 feet. - Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 7:30 PM EST Thursday was 9.1 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to remain nearly steady around 9.1 through the weekend and into next week. - Flood stage is 8.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

title: Flood Warning
description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas... Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County. For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers, Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Minor flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast. * WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden. * WHEN...From Sunday afternoon until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Much of the flood plain below cotulla to below tilden is cut off, as sloughs and peripheral channels fill. Hunting cabins, oil field pump jacks and tank batteries flood well away from the channel. Livestock are cut off and can drown. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 6:30 PM CST Thursday the stage was 9.3 feet. - Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early Sunday afternoon and continue rising to a crest of 15.0 feet Monday morning. - Flood stage is 14.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
